e4: White claims the centre with the king's pawn and opens lines for the bishop and the queen. It is the most popular first move.
e4 e5: Black answers symmetrically, taking a share of the centre and keeping the position open and classical.
e4 e5 Nf3: The knight develops and attacks the e5 pawn at the same time, so Black has to answer the threat.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6: Black defends e5 with the knight, which also develops a piece toward the centre.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4: The Italian bishop aims at the f7 square, Black's weakest point early on, and prepares to castle quickly.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5: The Ruy Lopez pins the knight that defends e5. White puts pressure on Black's centre without taking anything yet.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4: The Scotch challenges e5 at once and opens the centre, giving White active pieces and open lines.
e4 e5 Nc3: The Vienna develops the knight first and prepares f4 later, keeping the choice between quiet play and an attack.
e4 e5 f4: The King's Gambit offers the f-pawn to pull Black's e-pawn away and take control of the centre with an attack.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6: Petrov's Defense counterattacks e4 instead of defending e5, leading to a solid and symmetrical game.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3: White develops the second knight and defends e4, heading for a solid symmetrical position.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6: Black copies White and develops the second knight, which also attacks the e4 pawn.
e4 e5 Nf3 d6: Philidor's Defense defends e5 with a pawn. It is solid but gives Black less space.
e4 c5: The Sicilian fights for the centre from the side by attacking d4, and leads to unbalanced positions.
e4 c5 d4: White offers the d-pawn. If Black takes it, White gets quick development and open lines in return.
e4 e6: The French prepares ...d5 with a solid pawn chain, accepting a slightly cramped position for a sturdy structure.
e4 c6: The Caro-Kann prepares ...d5 with the c-pawn, which keeps the bishop on c8 free to leave the pawn chain.
e4 d5: The Scandinavian challenges e4 at once. Black accepts an early queen move in return for fast central contact.
e4 Nf6: Alekhine's Defense attacks e4 right away and invites White to advance the pawns, which Black will then try to attack.
e4 d6: The Pirc waits to take the centre. Black lets White build it and plans to attack it with pieces and flank pawns.
e4 d6 d4: White takes a big centre with the e- and d-pawns, the usual plan against the Pirc.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6: Black develops with an attack on the e4 pawn, forcing White to defend it or push forward.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3: White defends e4 with the knight and develops a piece at the same time.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6: Black prepares to put the bishop on g7, where it will press on White's centre from a distance.
d4: White takes space in the centre with the queen's pawn, opening lines for the queen and the bishop on c1.
d4 d5: Black copies White and holds the centre with a pawn of their own.
d4 d5 c4: The Queen's Gambit offers the c-pawn to undermine Black's d5 pawn and to win control of the centre.
d4 d5 c4 e6: The Queen's Gambit Declined supports d5 with a pawn. It is solid, but the bishop on c8 is shut in for now.
d4 d5 c4 dxc4: Black accepts the pawn, but White usually wins it back and enjoys a strong centre in the meantime.
d4 d5 c4 c6: The Slav supports d5 with the c-pawn and keeps the bishop on c8 free to develop outside the pawn chain.
d4 Nf6: Black develops a knight that controls e4, so White cannot take the full centre for free, and keeps the setup flexible.
d4 Nf6 Nf3: White develops the knight, controls e5 and prepares a flexible setup such as the London.
d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6: Black plans a fianchetto, putting the bishop on g7 to aim at the long diagonal.
d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4: The London bishop is developed outside the pawn chain before e3 closes the diagonal, and it controls e5.
d4 Nf6 c4: White adds the c-pawn to the centre and gains space on the queenside.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6: Black prepares the fianchetto of the king's bishop, the first step toward the King's Indian setup.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3: White develops a knight toward the centre and supports a later e4.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6: Black keeps the centre flexible and opens a path for the bishop, preparing a pin on the knight.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3: White develops the knight to the centre, which allows the Nimzo-Indian pin.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4: The Nimzo-Indian pins the knight on c3 so White cannot easily play e4. Black fights for the centre with pieces.
c4: The English opens on the flank, controls the d5 square and keeps White flexible about the central pawn structure.
Nf3: The Réti develops a knight first, controls e5 and d4 and keeps White's pawn structure open to many plans.
Nf3 d5: Black takes the centre at once, so White will usually fight it with flank pawns.
Nf3 d5 c4: White attacks Black's d5 pawn from the flank, and the opening resembles a Queen's Gambit with extra flexibility.
d4 f5: The Dutch fights for e4 with the f-pawn. It gives Black an ambitious kingside play and a slightly weakened king.
